1. Two medicines in one injection. CagriSema combines cagrilintide, an amylin analogue, with semaglutide, the GLP-1 drug in Ozempic and Wegovy.
  2. Not approved yet. Novo Nordisk filed with the US FDA in December 2025, and a decision is expected in the last quarter of 2026.
  3. Strong trial results. In the main phase 3 trial, people lost 20.4% of their body weight on average over 68 weeks, compared with 3% on placebo.
  4. Not available as a medicine in Indonesia. In Bali, cagrilintide is available only as a research compound.

CagriSema is Novo Nordisk’s next weight-management injection, and one of the most talked-about drugs in the GLP-1 field. Its name joins its two ingredients: cagrilintide and semaglutide.

The short answer to the title: CagriSema is a once-weekly combination injection that is still waiting for its first approval. Below, we explain what it contains, where its approval stands, what the trials showed, and what the amylin part adds.

What Does CagriSema Contain?

CagriSema is a fixed combination of two active ingredients, given together as one injection once a week. Each ingredient copies a different natural hormone involved in appetite.

Cagrilintide: A Long-Acting Amylin Analogue

Cagrilintide copies amylin, a hormone your pancreas releases alongside insulin after meals. Amylin helps you feel full and slows how quickly food leaves your stomach. Cagrilintide is a long-acting version that lasts long enough for weekly dosing. During development, it was known by the research codes AM833 and NN9838.

Semaglutide: The GLP-1 Part

Semaglutide is the GLP-1 receptor agonist already sold as Ozempic and Wegovy. It copies GLP-1, a gut hormone that lowers blood sugar and reduces appetite. We explain how semaglutide works in a separate guide.

Is CagriSema Approved Yet?

Not yet. As of early November 2026, CagriSema has not been approved by any regulator, and the first decision is due in the US.

United States: FDA Decision Expected in Late 2026

Novo Nordisk submitted its application to the FDA on 18 December 2025. It asked for approval to help adults with obesity, or with overweight and at least one weight-related condition, lose weight and keep it off, alongside diet and exercise. In its 4 November 2026 results, Novo listed the US decision for the last quarter of 2026 and said it is preparing for a US launch in early 2027, subject to approval.

Other Countries

Novo has also filed CagriSema with China’s drug regulator and expects that review to finish in the first half of 2028. The company’s November 2026 report did not mention a filing in the European Union.

Indonesia

CagriSema is not registered with BPOM, and we found no announcement of an Indonesian filing. Like any new medicine, it would need its own BPOM approval before it could be prescribed here.

What Did the CagriSema Trials Show?

CagriSema has been tested in the REDEFINE trials for weight management and the REIMAGINE trials for type 2 diabetes. These are the main results reported so far:

Trial Who took part Length Average weight loss
REDEFINE 1 3,417 adults with obesity or overweight and a related condition, without diabetes 68 weeks 20.4% on CagriSema, versus 14.9% on semaglutide alone, 11.5% on cagrilintide alone and 3.0% on placebo
REDEFINE 2 1,206 adults with type 2 diabetes and obesity or overweight 68 weeks 13.7% on CagriSema, versus 3.4% on placebo
REDEFINE 9 Adults with obesity 68 weeks 21% on a lower-dose version of CagriSema
REIMAGINE 5 Adults with type 2 diabetes, compared with tirzepatide 60 weeks 12.4% on a lower-dose CagriSema, versus 9.1% on a low dose of tirzepatide

REDEFINE 1 and REDEFINE 2 were published in the New England Journal of Medicine in June 2025, and they form the basis of the FDA application. In REDEFINE 1, 40.4% of people on CagriSema lost at least a quarter of their body weight.

The side effects looked like those of other GLP-1 medicines. About 80% of people on CagriSema in REDEFINE 1 had a stomach or gut side effect, such as nausea, constipation or vomiting, compared with about 40% on placebo. Most were mild to moderate, and 5.9% stopped treatment because of side effects, compared with 3.5% on placebo.

What Does an Amylin Analogue Add to a GLP-1 Drug?

Amylin and GLP-1 are both fullness hormones, but they work through different signals. GLP-1 slows digestion and acts on appetite centres in the brain. Amylin, released together with insulin, sends its own fullness signal to the brain and also slows stomach emptying. Adding an amylin analogue to a GLP-1 drug aims to reduce appetite through two routes at once.

REDEFINE 1 is the clearest test of that idea, because it compared the combination with each ingredient alone. CagriSema led to 20.4% average weight loss, more than semaglutide alone (14.9%) or cagrilintide alone (11.5%). For people already familiar with semaglutide, that difference is what the amylin part brings.

Is CagriSema Available in Bali?

Not as a medicine. CagriSema has no approval anywhere yet, so no pharmacy in Indonesia can dispense it on prescription.

What you can find in Bali is cagrilintide as a research compound, supplied for laboratory and research use. We supply cagrilintide in Bali on that basis. Our cagrilintide is sold for research use only. It is not CagriSema, it is not a Novo Nordisk product, it is not a BPOM-registered medicine, and it is not approved for human use.

Conclusion

CagriSema is a once-weekly injection that combines cagrilintide, a long-acting amylin analogue, with semaglutide, the GLP-1 drug in Ozempic and Wegovy. In its main trial, people lost 20.4% of their body weight on average over 68 weeks, more than with either ingredient alone, with mostly mild to moderate stomach side effects.

It is not approved yet. Novo Nordisk filed with the FDA in December 2025, expects a US decision in the last quarter of 2026, and has also filed in China. In Indonesia, CagriSema is not registered as a medicine, while cagrilintide is available in Bali as a research compound, supplied for research use only.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who Makes CagriSema?

Novo Nordisk, the company behind Ozempic and Wegovy. CagriSema is its first combination of a GLP-1 drug and an amylin analogue.

When Will CagriSema Be Available?

Not before a regulator approves it. Novo expects a US decision in the last quarter of 2026 and plans a US launch in early 2027 if it is approved. There is no announced timeline for Indonesia.

Is CagriSema a Pill or an Injection?

It is an injection, given once a week, with both ingredients combined in a single dose.

Does CagriSema Work Better Than Semaglutide Alone?

In REDEFINE 1, yes. People on CagriSema lost 20.4% of their body weight on average, compared with 14.9% on semaglutide alone over the same 68 weeks.

How Does CagriSema Compare With Tirzepatide?

Only early comparisons are available. In REIMAGINE 5, a diabetes trial using lower doses of both drugs, CagriSema led to 12.4% weight loss versus 9.1% with tirzepatide over 60 weeks.

What Are the Side Effects of CagriSema?

Mostly stomach and gut effects, such as nausea, constipation and vomiting. In REDEFINE 1, most were mild to moderate, and 5.9% of people stopped treatment because of side effects.
